title: Cancer screening availability and subsidies under Healthier SG
asked: Mr Vikram Nair asked whether there are plans to increase the availability and uptake of screening for common cancers such as lung, liver and prostate cancer, given rising cancer detection in Singapore.
response: Ms Rahayu Mahzam said cancer screening uptake is a matter of health habits. Under Healthier SG, breast, cervical and colorectal screening is recommended and heavily subsidised. Lung and liver screening is only recommended for high-risk individuals because general population screening has lower yield and can cause false positives. MOH also promotes healthier lifestyles to address modifiable cancer risk factors.

key_points.point: Under Healthier SG, regular screening for breast, cervical and colorectal cancer is recommended and heavily subsidised.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Under Healthier SG, regular screening for common cancers, such as breast, cervical and colorectal cancer, is recommended and heavily subsidised

key_points.point: Lung and liver cancer screening is only recommended for high-risk individuals.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: As for screening for lung and liver cancer, it is only recommended for high-risk individuals.

key_points.point: General population screening for these cancers has lower yield and can lead to many false positives.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: general population screening has lower yield compared to more targeted screening and can lead to many false positive results

key_points.point: MOH promotes healthier lifestyles such as not smoking, limiting alcohol, healthy diets and physical activity.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: has been promoting healthier lifestyles, for example, not smoking, limiting alcohol consumption, healthy diets and physical activity

key_points.point: For the general population, screening recommendations are highly subsidised.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we make recommendations and these are highly subsidised

key_points.point: Recommendations reference the Screening Test Review Committee.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we actually make reference to the recommendations by the Screening Test Review Committee

key_points.point: For individuals, prevalence and clinical effectiveness differ, and patients are encouraged to have a good relationship with their doctors.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: What we recommend is for patients to have that good relationship with their doctors so that they can individually recommend it accordingly.

key_points.point: Making a scheme for individual screening would require separate resourcing.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: To make a scheme out of this is something we need to assess because it will require some separate resourcing.
